defects.summary: D1's new primary guard re-opens D2's exact defect on the primary side: --check-current prints `--repin` (and the federated `--repin --ref <branch> --repin-source ...`) for a lock whose primary ref is a branch name, and the same generator now refuses that command at exit 1. Unlike the source side this shape needs no hand edit — `--ref main` is a supported invocation — and the round's own newly-reworded cross-repo contract fact (3) asserts the opposite.
defects.evidence:
The D2 fix consults `repin_source_blocker` only in check_current's SOURCE branch (generate_skills_lock.py:2152). The PRIMARY branch prints unconditionally at :2134, and D1's new guard at :1919 refuses the printed command.

REPRODUCED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v4/primary_deadend.py — no hand edit anywhere:
  generate --ref main: exit 0, lock ref: main
  check-current exit 1 -> "FAILED: the bundle has moved on since main … Re-pin it … with:"
    python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin
  RAN that line verbatim -> exit 1 | ERROR: … pins 'Acme/registry' at 'main', which is not a commit sha …

SECOND MANIFESTATION, harness scratchpad/v4/fed_primary_branch.py — primary at a branch, source at a sha, only the source drifted. `repin_source_blocker` returns None (it inspects the SOURCE's ref only), so the federated command is printed with the branch as its anchor and is refused by the same primary guard:
  printed: python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref main --repin-source 'file:///…/cms-platform@'
  RAN -> exit 1 | ERROR: … pins '…/registry' at 'main', which is not a commit sha …

THE PROSE HALF, in the change whose subject is false prose. 3599c21 strengthened contract fact (3) at :2046-2051 from "its own remediation line" to "Either the line IMMEDIATELY under its headline is the command that fixes it, or there is no command to print and the headline says so itself". For both shapes above the line immediately under the headline is a command that does not fix it — it exits 1 — and the headline says nothing. The sentence is false as written, and 12c2095 is the commit that made it false.

The D2 comment at :2141-2150 states the rule this violates in its own words: "a report that prints the command anyway sends its reader — or the fleet bumper … — to an exit 1 with nothing else offered." Neither new test covers it: test_check_current_prints_no_repin_command_the_flag_would_refuse uses only `_lock_federating_one_registry_twice`, and test_repin_refuses_a_primary_pinned_at_a_branch never runs --check-current.

defects.summary: The D2 fix's shared predicate is not the whole refusal: `repin_source_blocker` omits `_apply_repin_sources`' primary-registry rejection, so on a lock naming one registry as BOTH its primary and a federated source, --check-current still prints a `--repin-source` the flag refuses at exit 1. The new docstring enumerates which refusals it leaves out and justifies the omission with a claim that is false for this one.
defects.evidence:
`_apply_repin_sources` refuses three things before merging: the primary registry (:920-924), an unknown registry (:925-930), and whatever `repin_source_blocker` returns (:933). check_current consults only the third (:2152). The blocker's docstring at :810-813 addresses the gap and gets it wrong: "None for a registry this lock does not federate at all: refusing THAT is `_apply_repin_sources`' own 'ADDING a source' case … and check_current only ever asks about a source it has just read." It never mentions the primary-registry refusal, and the trailing clause is exactly why that refusal IS reachable — check_current asked about a source it had just read, and the flag rejected it.

REPRODUCED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v4/bothhalves.py, on the same lock shape round 1's atk/f_layoutclaim.py already established as representable (one registry as primary with bundle `adam` and as a source with bundle `other`; `--check` green, plan_sources' uniqueness check is keyed on bundle):

    python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref 74926093… --repin-source 'file:///…/registry@'
  RAN that line verbatim -> exit 1 | ERROR: --repin-source file:///…/registry is this lock's PRIMARY registry, not a federated source; the primary's pin is what --ref (or bare --repin) advances

Note `--only` is NOT an escape here — `_select_sources` (:1445) refuses to scope to a registry that is both halves — so this drift is reported by the unscoped run alone and has no command the tool accepts. Same class as the defect a79961a claims to have closed, one shape over, and untested: no test runs --check-current against a lock whose source shares the primary's registry.

defects.summary: Both refusal messages D1 added tell the reader to repair the lock with a plain generate, and following either literally silently de-federates the lock at exit 0 — the precise hazard this file warns about 200 lines away and that the sibling refusal in the same function is carefully worded to avoid.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:865-868 (source side) advises `--source '<one entry>'`; :1925-1927 (primary side) advises "a plain generate (--registry / --ref / --bundles)". A plain generate takes `sources` from the command line alone.

MEASURED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v4/defed.py — lock with srcA (hand-edited to 'main') and srcB:
  refusal names: --source 'srcA=file:///…/srcA@<sha>:<layout>'
  followed literally -> exit 0, "Wrote …: 2 skills"
  sources before: ['…/srcA', '…/srcB'] ; sources after: ['…/srcA'] ; srcB DROPPED AT EXIT 0: True

And scratchpad/v4/defed2.py — federated lock generated by the supported `--ref main`:
  refusal names: a plain generate (--registry / --ref / --bundles)
  followed literally -> exit 0, "Wrote …: 1 skills"
  sources after: <ABSENT> ; WHOLE FEDERATED ARRAY DROPPED AT EXIT 0: True

The file already knows this. At :2129-2132: "--repin, not a bare re-run: this lock may federate, and a plain generate takes `sources` from the command line alone, so following that instruction literally would de-federate it at exit 0. The remediation line is the one place a reader is told which command to type, so it must name the safe one." And `repin_source_blocker`'s OTHER message, six lines above the new one, says "restate the whole ARRAY with a plain generate" — the qualifier the new messages drop.

This compounds defect 1: for a federated lock whose primary ref is a branch name, `--repin` is now hard-refused and the only route the tool offers is the one that silently drops the federated half, after which `--check` is green for having done so.

defects.summary: The `_COMMIT_SHA_RE` comment claims the sha-vs-ref distinction is "load-bearing on the --repin path alone", but the regex also decides what --check-current PRINTS — and it did so already in the commit that wrote the sentence.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:392-393: "The distinction is load-bearing on the --repin path alone" (and :402-403, "--repin is the one mode that treats it as one"). The regex's only two uses are :859, inside `repin_source_blocker`, and :1919. But `repin_source_blocker` is read by check_current at :2152 — a read-only mode — and a79961a (the D2 commit that wired that call) is the PARENT of 12c2095 (the D1 commit that added the regex and this comment), so the sentence was false the moment it was written.

MEASURED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v4/checkcurrent_sha_dep.py — a drifted source hand-pinned at 'main', plain `--check-current`, no --repin anywhere:
  COMMAND PRINTED: False
  headline carries "… would refuse one: this lock pins that source at 'main', which is not a commit sha …"
Flip `_COMMIT_SHA_RE` and that output changes, so the regex is load-bearing on a second path.

Same line, smaller: the headline reads "moved on since 6d93d2238c10…, which <lock> still pins for it" and then, in the same sentence, "this lock pins that source at 'main'". The first half names the RESOLVED ref as what the lock pins, which for this shape it does not — two different pins asserted one clause apart.

defects.summary: `_COMMIT_SHA_RE` is lowercase-only, so a 40-hex sha in uppercase — which git resolves and which is a commit sha — is refused with a message telling the reader it "is not a commit sha".
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:404: `_COMMIT_SHA_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}")`, used with `.fullmatch` at :859 and :1919. `validate_ref`'s `_REF_RE` accepts `[A-Za-z0-9._/+:@-]+`, so an uppercase sha reaches the lock intact.

MEASURED, harness /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agentskills/0ad08fc2-e344-5f69-99ba-9468ecf58a91/scratchpad/v4/upper.py:
  git resolves UPPERCASE sha: True   (`git cat-file -e <UPPER>^{commit}` exit 0)
  HEAD --repin on uppercase-sha lock: exit 1 | ERROR: … pins 'Acme/registry' at 'B7E08C566B1A1C92B7B4D9366E683DFCA86D185B', which is not a commit sha …

The refusal is arguably fine as a normalization rule — this generator only ever writes lowercase — but the sentence a reader is handed is one they can check and find false, and the remediation it then offers is the de-federating advice of defect 3. Either widen to `[0-9a-fA-F]{40}` or say "not a sha this generator writes".
